description: Sclerotinia timber rot is a fungal disease that causes severe stem decay in many crops. The fungus produces white cotton-like mold and black survival bodies called sclerotia. Infected stems become dry or rotten, leading to plant wilting and collapse.
symptoms: White cotton-like fungal growth on stems
Stem rot or dry decay (timber-like appearance)
Black seed-like sclerotia inside or on stems
Plants collapsing due to stem damage
visual_symptoms: black hard sclerotia in infected tissue
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil as sclerotia for several years
Sclerotia germinate and produce apothecia (small cup-like structures)
Spores infect plant tissues during wet conditions
New sclerotia develop in infected stems and fall into the soil
impact: Severe yield losses in susceptible crops
cultural_control: Improve spacing and airflow between plants
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
biological_control: Apply biological agents such as Coniothyrium minitans
Use beneficial fungi like Trichoderma species
prevention: Use clean seeds and healthy transplants
Monitor crops during cool and wet weather
